title: Saudi Aramco's Jazan REFINERY (400,000 b/d, Red Sea coast) hit Thu Nov 26: the Energy Ministry says a 'hostile aerial projectile' sparked a fire and some operations were suspended; one Nepali worker killed, several injured; the coalition blames the Houthis; damage assessment under way; not the Jazan PORT hit of Nov 25
body:
# Jazan refinery, Thu Nov 26 (late, carded at the night boot)

| State | Read | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| ATTACKED | Saudi Energy Ministry: the facility was hit by a 'hostile aerial projectile', which sparked a fire | Arab News 11/26 (page read, published 15:19Z) quoting the ministry statement; Reuters title in the lane 20:56Z 'Attack on Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery kills worker, halts some operations' (page not read) |
| SHUT, partly | 'led to the suspension of some operations'; which units and for how long NOT STATED; no restart timeline found | same; search summaries say the fire was brought under control (outlet not read) |
| DAMAGED | not quantified: 'emergency and technical teams ... complete a damage assessment and safety checks' | Arab News |
| Casualties | one Nepali worker killed, several injured of different nationalities | ministry via Arab News |
| Attribution | ministry did not name the attacker; the coalition says the Houthis did it and that it destroyed a ballistic missile launch platform at Hodeidah used in the attack; no Houthi statement found | Arab News; Cyprus Mail via search summary |
| Capacity | up to 400,000 b/d crude processing (CAPACITY, not a loss figure) | Arab News |

- **Guards applied (IRAN_WAR_GUARDS):** this is the REFINERY, not Jazan PORT (card 20261125-042, minor damage, no casualties): do not merge them. 400,000 b/d is capacity: a loss figure has not been stated by anyone. ATTACKED / SHUT (partly) / DAMAGED (not quantified) are carried separately. The 2019 Abqaiq number does not attach. The guard file's older line 'Jizan shut since 7/27, restart never confirmed' (ADD#19, August) conflicts with 'suspension of some operations' today, which implies units were running: FALCON settles the prior state.
- **Not adjudicated here:** whether a refinery hit moves any FALCON rung (FAL-01 is RESOLVED; the live D 85 to 92 rung covers Gulf-ally PRODUCTION, and refining is not production in this file's record); FALCON grades. Brent effect is BRENT's (CNBC 04:46Z had BZ 94.71 before this event; no later read here; US markets shut Thursday).
- **Late:** public from about 15:19Z (10:19 ET); carded at the night boot: no WALTER session ran on Thanksgiving until 22:22 ET (clock stamp). Same day: Houthi claim on Ras Tanura (card 20261125-008), Jazan port (042), two Italians killed in Kuwait (card 20261126-004).
- **So what:** the Saudi Red Sea side, the bypass for Hormuz, now has a confirmed hit with a fatality on an Aramco processing asset, one day after the port hit. The next things that matter: which units stopped and for how long (Aramco or ministry), and whether Yanbu or Rabigh follows.
source: arabnews.com 'Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery kills Nepali worker' (published 2026-11-26T15:19Z, read 2026-11-26 ET); Research-Intake data/2026-11-26/news.json titles (Reuters 20:56Z, Al Jazeera 20:38Z, NBC 20:44Z); search summaries (Cyprus Mail, Archyde)

dispatch_note: IMMEDIATE: a confirmed hit with a fatality and partial shutdown on a Saudi Red Sea Aramco asset (LAST_COMPLETION resume list item 1 class). Same recipients as 042. Iran pre-dispatch guard: IRAN_WAR_GUARDS.md read whole this session; anchor full sweep 11/23, this is a state change for the ~11/30 sweep. RED, PROME by BOARD diff.
route_summary: Jazan refinery hit, worker killed, some operations suspended

title: Kuwait, Thu Nov 26: two Italian technicians of Rheinmetall, supporting air-defence systems, killed at a 'vital site'; Kuwait's army and Italy blame Iran, Italy says the drone was Iranian-made; Iran's foreign minister calls it 'suspicious' and denies an operation; Kuwait's defence ministry first said drones were intercepted and four hurt by shrapnel; plus an Iranian Army mine claim for Nov 25
body:
# Kuwait strike and a Hormuz mine claim, Nov 25 to 26

| # | Item | Read | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Kuwait strike | Two Italian nationals, Rheinmetall technicians 'providing technical support for air defence systems', died after a strike on a Rheinmetall facility in Kuwait. Kuwait's army: a 'vital site', 'heinous Iranian aggression'. Earlier, Kuwait's defence ministry: drones from Iran detected and INTERCEPTED, four people (the two Italians, a Kuwaiti, a Pakistani) injured by falling shrapnel. Italy's foreign minister (Italian media): the drone was made in Iran, proxies known to attack. Iran: FM Araghchi 'suspicious', 'precooked recipe for war', condolences; armed forces spokesman Shekarchi: 'no military or offensive operations have been conducted'. Rheinmetall statement confirms the deaths | BBC 11/26 (page read, published 15:36Z); Arab News 11/26 (page read) |
| 2 | Context | BBC: just over a week after Kuwait said it repelled Iranian drone attacks on an airbase hosting US forces, the first strikes on Kuwait in more than two months | BBC |
| 3 | Mine claim, Hormuz | Iranian Army statement via Fars: an oil tanker hit a naval mine and caught fire in a 'restricted zone' in the strait on Wed 11/25; state media earlier said two tankers struck mines and exploded. Vessel unnamed, no UKMTO or neutral confirmation found. May be the same as or new beside the 11/24 IRGC claims on card 20261125-002: not established | CNBC/Reuters 11/26 04:46Z (page read) |

- **Guards applied (IRAN_WAR_GUARDS):** item 1: 'intercepted' and 'killed' are both on record from Kuwait's own statements; carry both, do not let the retelling become 'Iranian drone strike destroys facility'. Casualty counts carried with their sources, nothing adjudicated. Item 3: a mine claim relayed from Iranian state channels does NOT fire GATE 2 or any FALCON rung on relay (7/27 Tasnim guard); vessel, position and event time are the discriminators (ADD#26), and none is published.
- **Not on the anchor before:** a Kuwait in-port hit is a re-verify trigger; this is not a port, and the site is unnamed. Deaths of NATO-country nationals at a German defence contractor's site is the new element; HAWK owns the cross-war read.
- **Late:** BBC 15:36Z; carded at the night boot.
- **So what:** Iran-attributed fire on a Gulf state killed Western contractors the same day the Houthis hit Jazan refinery (card 003); Iran's denial frames it as a provocation. Escalation risk on both Gulf legs at once; FALCON and HAWK grade.
source: bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c39w9y5dx4k5o (published 2026-11-26T15:36Z, read 2026-11-26 ET); arabnews.com Jazan article (same day, mentions Kuwait); cnbc.com 2026/11/26 oil article (04:46Z, read); FT title 'Two Italians killed in drone strike on Kuwait' (20:23Z, not read)
confidence_language: confirms: deaths on record from Kuwait's army, Italy's foreign ministry and Rheinmetall (via BBC); attribution disputed; mine claim is Iranian state media only
dispatch_note: PRIORITY: confirmed fatal strike on a Gulf state attributed to Iran by two governments, denied by Iran; Hormuz mine claim carried as claim only. Iran pre-dispatch guard read this session. PROME by BOARD diff.
route_summary: Kuwait: two Italian contractors killed, Iran blamed and denies; Iranian mine claim
